record.original_question: In axion-like particle scenarios where the first phase transition occurs during inflation, phase fluctuations δθ = H_infl/(2πf) can generate large-scale variations that are constrained by the observed isotropy of the cosmic microwave background. What mechanism suppresses the excluded large-scale fluctuations, and can a large inflation-stage amplitude φ of the complex ALP field that later decreases to the broken-symmetry value f provide a viable solution?

evidence.quote: Quantum fluctuations lead to variations in phase between disconnected regions. These fluctuations are given by δθ = Hinfl / 2πf, where Hinfl is Hubble parameter at the inflationary stage [1].

The open question in the scenario with the first phase transition at the inflationary stage is the necessity to suppress large scale fluctuations, excluded by the observed CMB isotropy. One of the possible solution can be a large amplitude ϕ of the complex ALP field (1) at the stage of inflation, corresponding to the modern horizon, and its decrease down to the broken symmetry value f (see Eq.(3)) at successive inflationary stages.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider an axion-like particle (ALP) model described by a complex scalar field Φ with a U(1) symmetry that is spontaneously broken at a scale f, so that after symmetry breaking Φ = (φ/√2) e^{iθ} with φ → f. Suppose the U(1)-breaking phase transition occurs during a de Sitter inflationary epoch with Hubble parameter H_infl. In disconnected Hubble patches, the ALP phase θ acquires independent quantum fluctuations of typical amplitude

  δθ = H_infl / (2π f).

If these phase fluctuations persist on scales corresponding to the present cosmological horizon, they would induce isocurvature/temperature anisotropies on the cosmic microwave background that exceed the observational bound on large-scale CMB isotropy.

Problem. Identify a dynamical mechanism within this ALP framework that suppresses the excluded large-scale phase fluctuations. In particular, analyze the proposal in which the radial amplitude φ of the complex ALP field takes a large value φ ≫ f during the early inflationary stage corresponding to the present horizon and subsequently relaxes to the broken-symmetry value f at later inflationary stages. Determine whether such a time-dependent radial amplitude φ(t) can reduce δθ = H_infl/(2π φ(t)) on horizon-scale modes to a level compatible with observed CMB isotropy while preserving the ALP scenario on smaller scales, and characterize the conditions on the potential of Φ, on H_infl, and on the duration of inflation under which this provides a viable solution.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem in a recent review of beyond-Standard-Model cosmology, suggesting a large inflation-stage amplitude that decreases to f as a possible mechanism but not establishing it. No definitive resolution was located in available sources.

status_evidence.title: Open questions of BSM Cosmology
status_evidence.snippet: The open question in the scenario with the first phase transition at the inflationary stage is the necessity to suppress large scale fluctuations, excluded by the observed CMB isotropy.
status_evidence.claim: The suppression mechanism for excluded large-scale ALP phase fluctuations is identified as an open question, with a large inflation-stage amplitude relaxing to f proposed as a possible solution.
